headline: SURGE BATTERY METALS POSTS $9.81B AFTER-TAX NPV AT NEVADA NORTH — 42-YEAR LITHIUM MINE BEATS PEA ON EVERY KEY METRIC
snippet: Surge Battery Metals (TSX-V: NILIF) released a Pre-Feasibility Study on October 2 showing an after-tax NPV of US$9.81 billion at an 8% discount rate, a 23.6% IRR, and Phase 1 capital of US$2.77 billion — with the 42-year, 111,400-tonne-per-year battery-grade lithium carbonate mine improving on the 2025 PEA across every metric. The JV with Evolution Mining is 67.5% owned by Surge; an analyst conference call to review results was held October 5.

headline: GOLD HART COPPER'S DDHTOL04 HITS 340M+ OF GOLD-COPPER PORPHYRY FROM SURFACE — ALL 4 CHILE HOLES RETURN 100M+ MINERALIZATION
source_name: Mining Stock Education / Gold Hart Copper
snippet: Gold Hart Copper Corp's fourth and final diamond drill hole at the Tolita gold-copper-molybdenum asset in Chile's Vicuña District intersected over 340 metres of gold-copper porphyry-style mineralization starting directly from surface — including 108m at 0.21 g/t AuEq from 0m depth. All four diamond holes drilled to date have returned at least 100m of gold-copper mineralization, with three returning 300m+, yet only 5% of the mapped Tolita anomaly has been tested.

headline: XCITE URANIUM ADDS SECOND RIG AND COMMENCES DRILLING AT BLACK BAY — FIRST HOLES BELOW 1.17% U3O8 SURFACE TRENCHES IN SASKATCHEWAN
snippet: Xcite Uranium commenced a six-hole, 1,300-metre diamond drilling program at the Black Bay project in Saskatchewan on October 5, adding a second rig to test conductors beneath a four-kilometre geophysical trend that returned up to 1.17% U3O8 in surface trenches. The C$1.1 million program drills adjacent to the former Black Bay uranium mine 20km south of Uranium City — with holes designed to determine whether the high surface grades extend at depth.

headline: CASCADIA MINERALS HITS 75.55M AT 1.19% COPPER AND 0.97 G/T GOLD IN YUKON — LARGEST CARMACKS DRILL PROGRAM SINCE 2007 EXTENDS KEY ZONE
snippet: Cascadia Minerals' drill hole CD-26-058 at its road-accessible Carmacks copper-gold project in central Yukon intersected 75.55 metres grading 1.19% copper, 0.97 g/t gold, 10.4 g/t silver and 335 ppm molybdenum — part of a 15,000-metre 2026 campaign, the largest drill program at Carmacks since 2007. The result continues to demonstrate expansion potential at a central Yukon project backed by a strategic investment from a major copper company.

headline: EVERGOLD HITS 7.70 G/T GOLD AND 186 G/T SILVER IN FIRST GOLDEN LION RESULTS — BC TOODOGGONE HIGH-GRADE SYSTEM GAINING DEFINITION
snippet: Evergold Corp released initial assay results from its 16-hole, 3,988-metre drill program at the Golden Lion project in British Columbia's Toodoggone district, with highlight hole GL26-031 intersecting 4.9 metres at 7.70 g/t gold and 186.0 g/t silver. Lead-zinc assays for the remaining 10 holes are still pending, which could extend the polymetallic profile of this epithermal system.

headline: GOLDERA EXPANDS EGAN GOLD TIMMINS CAMP — TWO NEW PARALLEL STRUCTURES DISCOVERED AHEAD OF Q4 DRILL PROGRAM
snippet: Goldera Exploration (TSX-V: GERA) reported that surface programs at the high-grade Egan Gold Project exposed two additional subparallel structures flanking the E1 zone — ahead of a Q4 2026 drill program designed to test all three simultaneously. Previous surface samples at E1 returned up to 105 g/t Au on a syenite-hosted system 35 km west of Timmins.

headline: AVANTI GOLD DRILLS 12.27M AT 5.39 G/T AU AT AKYANGA — BEST SECTION 3.78M AT 12.88 G/T CONFIRMS DEPTH EXTENSION
snippet: Avanti Gold Corp reported Phase I drill results at the Akyanga deposit showing MSDD0156 intersected 12.27 metres at 5.39 g/t gold — including 3.78 metres at 12.88 g/t — extending the known gold system below the pit-shell constraint. A second hole, MSDD0154, returned 17.25 metres at 2.44 g/t gold, confirming Akyanga remains open at depth with meaningful high-grade core widths.

headline: FREEPORT'S GRASBERG BLOCK CAVE WON'T REACH FULL OUTPUT UNTIL LATE 2027 — Q3 COPPER 830M LBS IN LINE, GOLD SALES DEFERRED 60,000 OZ
snippet: Freeport-McMoRan's October 2 Q3 update confirmed that the Grasberg Block Cave — the world's largest underground copper-gold mine — will not reach full production capacity until late 2027, following the September 2025 mud rush incident that has kept throughput at roughly 67% of normalized rates. Q3 copper came in at 830 million pounds in line with guidance, but 60,000 ounces of refined gold were deferred to Q4 due to processing timing at PT Freeport Indonesia, with the realized copper price exceeding $6.50 per pound.

headline: CANADIAN GOLDFIELDS LAUNCHES AIRBORNE MAG SURVEY OVER 6,366-HA MIMINISKA GOLD PROJECT — FIRST DRILL TARGETS BEING DEFINED IN NW ONTARIO
snippet: Canadian Goldfields Discovery Corp. completed soil geochemistry sampling across the 6,366-hectare Miminiska Gold Project in northwestern Ontario and commenced a property-wide airborne magnetic survey on October 5, advancing target definition ahead of a first-pass drill campaign. The project sits in a region of northwestern Ontario prospective for structurally-controlled orogenic gold along the same geological corridors as established gold camps.

headline: SILVER ONE ADDS THIRD RIG AT CANDELARIA NEVADA — LATEST ASSAY EXTENDS SYSTEM 400M DOWN-DIP WITH 472 G/T SILVER OVER 9.14M
snippet: Silver One Resources (TSX-V: SVE) is accelerating its 25,000-metre drill program at the Candelaria silver-gold project in Nevada by adding a third rig in October, after the latest assay results extended the mineralized system 400 metres down-dip from the previously known area, returning 472 g/t silver over 9.14 metres within a broader 25.91-metre zone averaging 215 g/t Ag. With three rigs turning, Silver One targets completion of the 25,000-metre program in Q1 2027.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER HOLD FIRM ABOVE $4,100 AND $57 — BUT MINING STOCKS SLIDE UP TO 5X HARDER THAN SPOT METAL: TIME TO BUY?
snippet: Canadian Mining Report's October 2 analysis examines the widening divergence between firm gold (above $4,100) and silver (above $57) spot prices and underperforming mining equities — with some producers sliding two to five times harder than the metals themselves after the September payrolls shock. The piece identifies Blackrock Silver's Tonopah West at a projected AISC of US$17.44/silver-equivalent-ounce against a $60 silver price as a standout margin story, and frames the divergence as a potential reversion-to-mean entry window for investors with a 6-12 month horizon.
